item.text:
**4B.8 Research Note**
Overall read: **mixed, leaning positive on formal transfer; negative on succession maneuvering**. Jokowi clearly respected the constitutional end of his second term and the eventual transfer to Prabowo, but 2024 also featured credible evidence that his camp tried to reshape succession rules and preserve post-presidential influence.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| President Jokowi Calls on President, VP-Elect to Work Immediately after Inauguration | Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia | 2024-04-24 | <https://setkab.go.id/en/president-jokowi-calls-on-president-vp-elect-to-work-immediately-after-inauguration/> | Jokowi said the Constitutional Court process was “almost complete,” said the decision must be respected as final and binding, and said the cabinet would only assist a smooth transition rather than form a separate transition team. Strong positive evidence for respecting succession rules and constitutional transfer. | 4B.8 |
| Farewell-Welcome Ceremony for Indonesia’s President from Jokowi to Prabowo Subianto | Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia | 2024-10-20 | <https://setkab.go.id/en/farewell-welcome-ceremony-for-indonesias-president-from-jokowi-to-prabowo-subianto/> | The official record shows Jokowi welcoming Prabowo at the palace after inauguration, with the transition taking place on schedule on October 20, 2024. This is direct evidence that Jokowi completed a constitutional handover rather than resisting or delaying it. | 4B.8 |
| Indonesia court rejects election challenges, upholds Prabowo’s win | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-04-22 | <https://theprint.in/world/indonesia-court-rejects-election-challenges-upholds-prabowos-win/2051948/> | The Constitutional Court said there was no evidence of systematic fraud or presidential meddling and that state bodies had not been mobilized to sway the poll. This is the best formal-positive evidence that the election outcome and succession process were allowed to stand. | 4B.8 |
| Indonesia shelves plan to revise election law as protests rage | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-08-22 | <https://theprint.in/world/protests-across-indonesia-as-parliament-delays-change-to-election-law/2233305/> | Reuters reported that planned election-law changes would have benefited Jokowi’s youngest son, and that the push sparked protests and accusations of nepotism and democracy-destruction. This is strong negative evidence on respecting succession norms and not manipulating rules for family advantage. | 4B.8 |
| Indonesia lawmakers shelve plan to change election law as protests rage | Reuters | 2024-08-22 | <https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesia-shelves-plan-revise-election-law-protests-rage-2024-08-22/> | The Reuters report says the legislative fight centered on rules that would not apply under Jokowi’s term, but would shape the next cycle and had triggered public anger over attempts to consolidate power. This directly cuts against a clean “hands-off” succession record. | 4B.8 |
| Jokowi seeks Golkar takeover to retain decade-long influence | The Jakarta Post / Reuters | 2024-03-20 | <https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2024/03/20/jokowi-seeks-golkar-takeover-to-retain-decade-long-influence> | Reuters reported that Jokowi was trying to install a loyal ally to lead Golkar and secure a role on the party’s advisory board, preserving influence after leaving office. This is negative evidence for honoring coalition boundaries and leaving power cleanly. | 4B.8 |
| 'Jokowi effect': How Indonesia's outgoing leader shaped election to succeed him | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-02-12 | <https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/jokowi-effect-how-indonesias-outgoing-leader-shaped-election-to-succeed-him-3300317/> | Reuters said Jokowi had not formally endorsed a successor, but his son joining Prabowo’s ticket created a powerful perceived incumbent seal of approval and shifted coalition behavior. This is indirect negative evidence on clean succession, because it suggests his personal political weight was used to shape the successor race. | 4B.8 |
| Indonesia’s president-elect Prabowo secures parliamentary majority | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-08-16 | <https://theprint.in/world/indonesias-president-elect-prabowo-secures-parliamentary-majority/2225570/> | Reuters reported that NasDem joined Prabowo’s coalition, giving the incoming government a parliamentary majority and smoothing legislative processes before Jokowi left office. This is a limited positive signal that the transition was institutionally workable and not blocked by Jokowi. | 4B.8 |
| “I never asked for a third term as president:” Jokowi | The Jakarta Post | 2024-12-30 | <https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2024/12/30/i-never-asked-for-a-third-term-as-president-jokowi.html> | Jokowi denied making any proposal to serve beyond his second term. This is late but useful corroboration that there was no confirmed third-term bid in 2024, although it does not erase the succession-manipulation concerns above. | 4B.8 |

**Bottom line**
- **Positive:** Jokowi respected the formal two-term limit and completed a constitutional handover on October 20, 2024.
- **Negative:** his coalition and allied institutions were credibly reported to have maneuvered around succession rules and party control to preserve influence and advantage his son’s political path.

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong direct evidence of an explicit, formal third-term attempt in 2024.
- I also did not find evidence that Jokowi personally refused to transfer power, delayed inauguration, or ignored the court/KPU process.
- The strongest negatives are therefore **succession-rule manipulation and post-presidential influence-seeking**, not outright refusal of term limits.
